Those stable deltas/orders, the immediate synchronous probe count and every final per-case total stay frozen. The P-E-6 summary no longer asserts parking.exchange_entered_after_release: for the same scheduling reason, d1 can enter its exchange before d2's refusal settles or after the finally releases parking. The flag stays a raw observation; parking.released stays frozen.

decisions.text: Node binding SDK factory. P-E redelivery uses k = 3, frozen in this header. The provenance recorder confirms db.isTransaction on the Node 26 runtime; lib/runtime-facts.mjs already does this and P-E relies on it.
The synthetic host database is harness-local node:sqlite under a dedicated scratch directory. It is neither Bloodtrail storage nor a Bloodtrail outbox, and it is deleted with the scratch.

P-E probe processes may add exactly --allow-fs-write=<scratch database directory>, plus read access to that same directory only if node:sqlite needs it. No other grant, and still no network grant. The pinned database_handling.permission_flags below are the exact planned flags.

P-E-9b relays through a bare handoff as drafted; composed retry is Stage 2. P-E-1f and P-E-6b stay under P-E (P-D already recorded PD-C9). P-E-3a's committed_and_durable reported for a not_committed occurrence is recorded as a finding against the Node binding's wording. P-E-x1 is kept as a supplementary measurement. The durabilityAttempted-without-exchange observation is a note for a later Node-binding change, not a case.
Owner macOS/Apple Silicon workstation, Node 26 outside the repository, distributable exact-head kit, no probe network. G38 names no model; every driver lane is recorded in driver_provenance.

The orchestrator may delegate S1 for #801-#804 only after head verification; the exact approval line and 'Delegated S1 under G39' are required. No approval is claimed or executed by this build; task 4.2 stays gated.
Per-run HMAC keys held only in memory; at most 10 runs of at most 5,000 occurrences each; synthetic data only.
The shared seven-day window opened at the owner's first run-approval comment, 2026-10-17T02:22:47Z, and closes 2026-10-24T02:22:47Z; expiry needs an amendment, never an extended timestamp.

definitions.boundaries: Boundary 1: each public SDK call outcome (returned result or thrown error), recorded as code/category/path; explicit acceptance is recorded where a refusal was expected. Boundary 2: the core sink interface, which receives each validated occurrence as a frozen canonical event; read through the testing capturing sink or the host's transaction-bound sink. Boundary 3: the exchange injected into the delivery handoff, including the handoff the transaction-critical binding is constructed with; each delivery attempt is recorded with its body SHA-256 and request metadata.
definitions.counters: probe: durabilityProbe invocations. gate: commitGate invocations; the gate is no-op when it only counts and returns 'committed'. exchange: exchange invocations, equal to delivery attempts. sink: core sink emits. business_commits: business rows/commits in the synthetic host database. seq: a monotonic event-order log using performance.now(); never event.timestamp. deliver/redeliver mean binding.deliver called again on the same instance with the same ev and transactionId, never core sdk.redeliver except P-E-10b(iii).
definitions.ordering: The binding pipeline order is probe, then gate, then handoff(event, 0). Under the truthful order the probe runs after the business commit it was meant to guard; the designed order (P-E-4b) can only be satisfied by an occurrence constructed before the commit.
definitions.redelivery: P-E-5 freezes k = 3: three 503 exchanges, then the acknowledgment on call k+1. A fail_closed result never settles the per-instance key, so every caller redelivery re-runs the probe and the commit gate; the binding schedules no retry.
definitions.classification: Each case is judged against the transaction_critical contract row (contract.source.json:595-604): holds / vacuous / not provided / SDK cannot detect / misrepresents. Step counters in the frozen plan are per-step deltas; per-case totals live in the summary actuals. A runtime mismatch is reported and never fixed by editing the expectation.

database_handling.ownership: harness-local synthetic host database, not Bloodtrail storage or outbox

findings.finding: The commit gate fails open on any value other than exactly 'declined': undefined and 'failed' proceed to the exchange as committed (delivery-classes.ts:350).
An outbox sink that defers its insert past a synchronous ROLLBACK persists an orphan row: the rollback variant leaves 0 business rows and 1 outbox row whose body says committed.
Two distinct occurrences sharing one transaction id run the commit gate twice: pair-key dedupe never makes the gate idempotent per transaction.
The binding reports committed_and_durable for a not_committed occurrence; the binding never reads commit_state or outcome, so its status label misrepresents the occurrence.

notes.note: durabilityAttempted can be true even when the handoff never called the exchange (request_too_large or request_serialization_failed, http-handoff.ts:100-106; delivery-classes.ts:354-356). An mfaRemoved occurrence cannot normally reach 64 KiB, so P-E does not test this; recorded for a later Node-binding change, not as a case.

On Node 26.12.0, node:sqlite wrote outside --allow-fs-write: new DatabaseSync created a file outside the write grant while fs.writeFileSync to the same path failed with ERR_ACCESS_DENIED. The grant confines only the harness's fs reserve (openSync 'wx') and unlink; database placement rests on p-e/host.mjs path checks before DatabaseSync construction. Network denial is unaffected (no --allow-net); neither SDK package imports node:sqlite.

cases.setup: h = sdk.beginOperation({boundEvent:'mfaRemoved'}).value; state 'started', transactional true, no business commit yet. await sdk.mfaRemoved({...MFA_INPUT, operation:h}) with no event.commit_state and no event.outcome. Follow-up: h.markCommitted(), then the same mfaRemoved call again.
cases.classification: Premature-success guard holds for the handle path (the transaction_critical row is not reached).

cases.setup: await sdk.mfaRemoved({...MFA_INPUT, event:{commit_state:'committed'}}) with no operation.
cases.classification: Premature-success guard holds for the direct path. Its path differs from P-E-1a: /event/commit_state vs /operation/state.

cases.setup: h = sdk.beginOperation({boundEvent:'mfaRemoved'}), not marked. await sdk.mfaRemoved({...MFA_INPUT, operation:h, event:{commit_state:'committed'}}).
cases.classification: Guard holds. The direct-value check takes precedence.

cases.setup: await sdk.mfaRemoved({...MFA_INPUT}) with no operation and no event fields.
cases.classification: Guard holds.

cases.setup: h = sdk.beginOperation({boundEvent:'mfaRemoved', transactional:false}), not marked. await sdk.mfaRemoved({...MFA_INPUT, operation:h}).
cases.classification: Guard holds through a second layer.

cases.setup: await sdk.mfaRemoved({...MFA_INPUT, event:{outcome:'failure'}}) with no operation.

corrected_from.old_text: Accepted: {ok:true, value:{status:'accepted'}}, sink events = 1. The captured occurrence has event.outcome 'failure' and event.commit_state 'committed', although no handle was ever transitioned.
corrected_from.reason: #797 (783196a) removed the outcome-derived commit default: resolveCommitState now refuses every transaction-bound event without operation evidence or a direct terminal commit state (events.ts:222-225), so no occurrence, sink call, probe, gate or exchange happens.

cases.classification: Corrected by #797: the guard now holds on the handle-less path too. The draft's 'SDK cannot detect' no longer applies; the transaction_critical row is not reached.

cases.setup: 1. h = beginOperation({boundEvent:'mfaRemoved'}). 2. Harness business commit: businessCommits=1, seq 'commit'. 3. h.markCommitted(). 4. r = await sdk.mfaRemoved({...MFA_INPUT, operation:h}). 5. ev = capturingSink.events[0]. 6. B = createTransactionCriticalDelivery({handoff, durabilityProbe: counting, resolves true}). 7. res = await B.deliver(ev, h.transactionId, countingGate returning 'committed'). The exchange acknowledges.
cases.classification: Contract row: durability 'atomic with successful business commit' is not established. The probe runs after the commit it was meant to guard.

cases.setup: Same as P-E-2, but durabilityProbe resolves false.
cases.classification: business_failure_posture 'fail_closed before business commit' is vacuous under the truthful order.

cases.setup: h = beginOperation({boundEvent:'mfaRemoved'}). Call h.markNotCommitted(), then emit. ev = captured. Then B.deliver(ev, h.transactionId, countingGate returning 'committed'). The exchange acknowledges.
cases.classification: The binding never reads commit_state or outcome, so its status label misrepresents the occurrence. Expected finding: committed_and_durable is reported for a not_committed occurrence.

cases.setup: Same as P-E-3a, but the gate returns 'declined', which is truthful because no business commit happened.
cases.classification: A truthful gate drops not-committed audit records. Only a gate that says 'committed' makes them durable.

cases.setup: h = beginOperation({boundEvent:'mfaRemoved'}). Call h.markCommitted() with no business commit. r = await sdk.mfaRemoved({...MFA_INPUT, operation:h}). ev = captured. Then B.deliver(ev, h.transactionId, countingGate), with the probe resolving false. Afterwards call h.markNotCommitted(), h.markCancelled(), and a plain re-emit on h. Then the corrected linkage follow-up: h2 = beginOperation({boundEvent:'mfaRemoved', transactionId:h.transactionId, correlationId:h.correlationId}); h2.markNotCommitted(); emit mfaRemoved({...MFA_INPUT, operation:h2, retry:{retry_attempt:1, original_event_id:<false event id>}}); beginOperation({operationId:h.operationId}); then B.deliver(corrective, h.transactionId, gate).

corrected_from.old_text: A corrective not_committed record needs a fresh handle, which gets a new operation_id and transaction_id, so nothing in the record links it to the false one.
corrected_from.reason: Review correction: beginOperation refuses only a reused operationId (sdk.ts:94-104). It accepts a caller-supplied transactionId and correlationId equal to h's (operations.ts:132-150), and buildCorrelation accepts retry.original_event_id pointing at the false occurrence (events.ts:227-253). The host can link the corrective record; the SDK just never requires or checks that link.

cases.classification: The SDK cannot detect this: an occurrence says committed although no commit happened. The SDK neither requires nor verifies any link between a false committed record and its correction; a link exists only if the host supplies it.

cases.setup: Call h.markCommitted() with no business commit, then emit. ev = captured. Then B.deliver(ev, h.transactionId, gate), where the probe resolves true and the gate performs the business commit and returns 'committed'. The exchange acknowledges. Variant: the gate's commit fails and returns 'declined'.
cases.classification: The binding's documented order can be satisfied only by an occurrence constructed before the commit, which is untruthful.

cases.setup: Truthful order (P-E-2) for ev and h, with businessCommits=1. On one binding B the exchange script is: calls 1..k return {kind:'response', status:503, acknowledgments:[]}, call k+1 acknowledges. k is frozen at 3. One initial B.deliver, then k redeliveries B.deliver(ev, h.transactionId, countingGate), then one more. After the initial failure, one observed quiet interval (a single macrotask turn, no delay) precedes caller redeliveries. This bounds the observation; it is not a persistence claim.
cases.classification: Contract row retry 'persistent retry after commit' is not provided. Retry is caller-driven and re-runs the probe and the commit gate on every attempt.

cases.setup: Truthful handle-backed occurrence. Create parking deferred BEFORE d1. Start d1 without awaiting it, await d2 for the same pair, explicitly release in finally, await d1 and deliver a third time.
cases.classification: holds: pair-key in-flight idempotency within one binding, not per-transaction gate idempotency.

cases.setup: One truthful occurrence and one binding. Sequentially deliver with the handle transaction id, then with pe-txn-other-0001. The occurrence and body remain untouched.
cases.classification: SDK cannot detect: caller-supplied transaction differs from the occurrence. Pair-key deduplication holds only per pair.

cases.setup: After P-E-2 succeeds on B1 (ev and h from the truthful order), create B2 = createTransactionCriticalDelivery({handoff, durabilityProbe}) and call B2.deliver(ev, h.transactionId, countingGate). Then call B1.deliver again.
cases.classification: Contract row idempotency is per instance and in memory only, so the same occurrence is delivered twice across instances or restarts.

cases.setup: Truthful order. The exchange returns {kind:'response', status:422, acknowledgments:[]}. Call B.deliver, then redeliver once. Variants: a 2xx with a mismatched acknowledgment, and a 3xx.
cases.classification: The binding result cannot tell a permanent rejection from a retryable outage.

cases.setup: Fresh host file and Node SDK with synchronous transaction-bound sink. BEGIN, business insert, markCommitted, mfaRemoved; record sink entry immediately before awaiting; await before COMMIT. Inspect snapshot/rows, then plain re-emit.
cases.classification: holds through host composition: business row and audit record commit atomically, not a binding guarantee.

cases.setup: Independently reproduce committed P-E-9 setup. Parse stored outbox text; create bare handoff with injected ACK and call handoff(parsed, 0) exactly once after COMMIT. No transaction-critical binding.
cases.classification: holds: byte identity across this host-outbox round trip and single bare handoff; no composed retry claim.

cases.setup: Fresh host/SDK: BEGIN, business insert, markCommitted, await accepted emit, ROLLBACK. Snapshot, plain re-emit, markNotCommitted, markCancelled, markCommitted, markCompensated, in that order.
cases.classification: durable atomicity holds through host composition; SDK cannot detect rollback: committed in-memory state and completed success diverge from zero durable rows. Compensation misrepresents a never-durable commit.

cases.setup: Five independent full P-E-10 replays, ending markCompensated. New BEGIN/business insert for i fresh handle, ii bounded retry on compensated h, iii pure retained redelivery, iii named retained redelivery, iv reused operationId; COMMIT each.

corrected_from.old_text: (ii) accepted with a new event id, correlation.retry_attempt 1 and original_event_id pointing to an occurrence that was never durable.
corrected_from.reason: Skeptic correction: P-E-10 ends compensated; a bounded retry on the compensated handle bypasses the duplicate guard but success/compensated fails commit validation, so PREMATURE_SUCCESS/validation at /event/commit_state. Options (i), both (iii) paths and (iv) are unchanged.

cases.classification: SDK cannot reverse completion after rollback; fresh handles or retained redelivery compose retries; ii cannot use the compensated handle.

cases.setup: Fresh host/SDK, first sink throws before insert. BEGIN/insert/markCommitted/emit/ROLLBACK/snapshot; second BEGIN/insert/plain emit on SAME committed handle/COMMIT/snapshot.
cases.classification: Reservation release follows sink failure, not SQL durability; contrasts with completed success in P-E-10.

cases.setup: Truthful order. Call B.deliver(ev, h.transactionId, gate) where the gate throws a synthetic Error. Variant: the probe throws. Then deliver again with the recovered no-op gate/probe.
cases.classification: The binding does not convert throwing injected callbacks into results, so results-not-exceptions does not hold at this boundary.

cases.setup: Truthful order (businessCommits=1). Variant A: durabilityProbe scripted [false, true], counting gate 'committed', acknowledging exchange; deliver, then redeliver. Variant B: probe always true, gate scripted ['declined', 'committed']; deliver, then redeliver.
cases.classification: Contract row retry is not provided; it is caller-driven. A fail_closed result never settles the key, so every redelivery re-runs the probe and the gate. Under the truthful order, 'fail_closed before business commit' is vacuous.

cases.setup: Truthful order, acknowledging exchange. (a) The gate resolves undefined, or 'failed' through a cast, instead of 'committed' or 'declined': one fresh binding per value, one deliver each. (b) The probe resolves a truthy non-boolean, 1 or 'no', through a cast: one fresh binding per value, one deliver each. (c) The probe resolves falsy non-booleans 0, '' and undefined, scripted across three delivers on one binding.
cases.classification: The commit-gate decision fails open: any value other than 'declined' is treated as committed. The probe decision is truthiness-based. Expected finding: the gate fails open on anything but exactly 'declined'.

cases.setup: Read a fresh binding's guarantees, Object.isFrozen(guarantees) and Object.keys(binding). Parent-only comparisons consume each owned row of P-E-2b/5/7/8 independently; tabulate every planned step against eight contract columns. All layout and analysis choices are implementer defaults; G-log supplies the Node factory for event-building peers.
cases.classification: Truthful-order before-commit refusal is vacuous (2b); standalone persistent retry/at-least-once is not provided (5); dedupe is per-instance (7); fail-closed can follow the gate (8); shutdown and backlog alert are not provided by this binding.

cases.setup: Fresh legitimate handle-backed committed MFA occurrence from the truthful order. Deliver with undefined and empty caller transaction ids, repeating each. SDK-construct authenticationFailed with authenticated actor, authoritative tenant, password authentication evidence and documentation source; deliver twice with a nonempty transaction id.

corrected_from.old_text: Use P-E-1f's accepted handle-free failure occurrence with no correlation.transaction_id.
corrected_from.reason: #797: core events.ts:223-225 now refuses P-E-1f PREMATURE_SUCCESS /operation/state, so no such occurrence exists. Refusal outcomes are unchanged; the old handle-free admission classification no longer applies.

cases.classification: holds: class and caller-id admission guards. SDK cannot detect caller/occurrence transaction mismatch (P-E-6b); admission never reads correlation.transaction_id.

cases.setup: Fresh handle marked not_committed, no business commit. Emit mfaRemoved twice on that handle, delivering each captured occurrence on one binding with one transaction id.
cases.classification: holds per pair; SDK cannot detect per-transaction gate non-idempotency. Expected finding: two occurrences with one transaction id run the gate twice. misrepresents: committed_and_durable labels not_committed occurrences.

cases.setup: Independent full P-E-10 replay including compensation; new BEGIN and fresh handle with old transactionId/correlationId, insert/markCommitted/emit/COMMIT.
cases.classification: Host can retry under the same transaction id; only operationId reuse is guarded.

cases.setup: Four independent full P-E-10 replays, ending compensated with completed success. Emit a plain, b failure, c failure/not_committed, d bounded retry linked to retained event.
cases.classification: not provided: mfa.removed has no compensated commit state. #812 consistency does not change these earlier validation/duplicate refusals.

cases.setup: Fresh host/SDK per rollback and commit variant. Sink enters synchronously then awaits Promise.resolve before insert. BEGIN/insert/markCommitted, call emit and immediately finish SQL synchronously without awaiting emit; then settle emit and snapshot, finally close/delete DB.
cases.classification: finding: deferred insert after rollback durably misrepresents business truth. Commit variant's two rows do not establish atomicity; host must await pending sink work. Expected finding: the deferred insert persists an orphan row.

cases.setup: Truthful order. The exchange (a) throws a synthetic Error or (b) resolves {kind:'timeout'}. Call B.deliver(ev, h.transactionId, countingGate), then redeliver once, per variant on its own binding.
cases.classification: Unlike P-E-x1, a failing exchange is converted into a result. Like P-E-8, the binding result cannot distinguish the cause.
